title: Known unit leak allowed joint recovery of coupling and noise in two fully observed passive worm models
abstract: We tested whether one covariance can determine symmetric circuit coupling and unknown independent current noise when all cells have a known unit leak. A linear system gives a unique solution if its noise-to-row-sum matrix is invertible. In 180 exact-covariance cases on two partial adult worm electrical maps with 180 cells each, the matrix was invertible and maximum relative off-diagonal coupling error was 3.184e-13. The maximum relative noise error was 8.608e-14. At coupling one and a 16-fold noise variance range, normalized inverse covariance had median coupling errors of 0.6676 and 0.6867. A 1% artificial covariance error raised joint-solution median errors to 0.1171 and 0.1431. Leak rates spread by plus or minus 10% around one gave median coupling errors near 0.0358 under the wrong unit-leak assumption. Independent Lyapunov and two-cell checks passed. The uniqueness statement is conditional; universal invertibility was not proved. These are assumed circuit-model results, not measured neural activity. Full observation, known leak, independent white drive, unit measurement gains and partial anatomy limit use. Original code, aggregate results, proof, figure and external retrieval steps support reproduction.

display.caption: Exact recovery and errors under covariance perturbation and wrong leak assumptions. Bands show the full range of ten assigned cases, not biological confidence intervals.
